name: Bratmobile
label: Kill Rock Stars
lede: Two dorm neighbors who couldn't quite play started a zine, then a "fake band," and ended up with the loudest, funniest, most quotable records of riot grrrl.

eras.title: A fake band with a zine
eras.text: Allison Wolfe and Molly Neuman meet as dorm neighbors in Eugene, start the fanzine Girl Germs, and play their first show before they can really play. By the end of 1991 they are a trio and one of the bands at the International Pop Underground Convention.

years.h: Wolfe and Neuman meet as dorm neighbors at the University of Oregon
years.p: [[Allison Wolfe|6ae4e39e-45fc-4276-94cd-bf149c20f7b9]] (from Olympia) and [[Molly Neuman|e4832571-a120-46fb-a5ff-1350f5ed2fce]] (from Washington, D.C.) both bring activist families and a love of punk, hip-hop and Beat Happening to Eugene.
years.xp: Wolfe has said she first noticed Neuman hogging a pay phone, mid breakup, with a fast-talking East Coast accent. Wolfe brought Olympia's K Records scene with her; Neuman brought Washington, D.C.

years.h: Girl Germs, the zine that names the scene
years.p: Wolfe and Neuman put out the first issue of Girl Germs, photocopied on Neuman's winter break at the Capitol Hill office of Arizona Representative Mo Udall.
years.xp:
It started as an idea for a radio show that never happened. The zine ran interviews with bands such as 7 Year Bitch, Jawbox and Unrest, and pieces from [[Kathleen Hanna|4638653b-a279-42d6-bd8c-b2bcb9a19f77]] and Mecca Normal's Jean Smith.

Copies now sit in archives at Duke, Barnard and the GLBT Historical Society in San Francisco.

years.cap: North Shore Surf Club, Olympia. Image needed.
q: We can't really play instruments exactly, but maybe we have something to say.
years.h: First show: five a cappella songs at the North Shore Surf Club
years.p: [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]] invites Wolfe and Neuman to play Olympia. They have no instruments, so they sing, then borrow gear from a Some Velvet Sidewalk member.
years.xp:
Wolfe has described the duo as a "fake band" at that point. Robert Christie of Some Velvet Sidewalk lent them equipment and told them to listen to the Ramones; Wolfe says she did the opposite and skipped the Ramones on purpose.

KEXP's interview tells it as an opening slot for [[Bikini Kill|1397d045-1603-41fc-80b9-712c18360145]].

years.h: A D.C. lineup with Christina Billotte and a tape called Bratmobile DC
years.p: Wolfe and Neuman recruit guitarist [[Erin Smith|d497afe0-b769-4af3-9c85-a012a4d166a8]], drummer [[Christina Billotte|62325e5d-014f-42a1-90d5-fa12e17aa214]] and artist Jen Smith, and rehearse at the Nation of Ulysses house, the Embassy.
years.xp: Calvin Johnson introduced Smith to Neuman at a Nation of Ulysses show in December 1990. The D.C. group recorded in the Embassy basement with Tim Green and issued the cassette Bratmobile DC.

years.h: Wolfe, Neuman and Erin Smith settle in as a trio
years.p: Smith on guitar, Neuman on drums, Wolfe on vocals: the lineup that makes every Kill Rock Stars-era record.

years.cap: International Pop Underground Convention, Olympia. Image needed.
years.h: The only band to play the Olympia convention twice
years.p: At the International Pop Underground Convention Bratmobile play twice, including a bill at Capitol Lake Park with the Melvins, Mecca Normal, Girl Trouble, Beat Happening and Fugazi.

eras.title: Pottymouth and a very public breakup
eras.text: The trio tours with Heavens to Betsy, records for John Peel and lands on Kill Rock Stars. It ends the way few bands do: on a New York stage in the middle of an argument.

years.h: On tour with Heavens to Betsy
years.p: Bratmobile head out on the road with [[Heavens to Betsy|8716a313-c6df-440c-9b74-370e8d79728e]], a bond that later produces a split 7-inch.
years.xp: Split singles with Tiger Trap, Heavens to Betsy, Brainiac and Veronica Lake are part of the early catalog.

years.h: Tim Green records most of Pottymouth in the Embassy for pizza and hair dye
years.p: Green of Nation of Ulysses takes a slice of cheese pizza and a bottle of black hair dye as payment.
years.xp: The album was pieced together over sessions from August 1991 to July 1992. Three songs came earlier from Egg Studios in Seattle and YoYo Studios in Olympia.

years.h: Pottymouth: 17 songs in under 28 minutes
years.p: The debut album on Kill Rock Stars runs 27:47. Robert Christgau singled out tracks, and AllMusic's Stewart Mason called it a snapshot of the early 90s indie scene.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes retrospective rankings, including a place on Rolling Stone's 2026 greatest punk albums list.

years.h: A session for John Peel on the BBC
years.p: The band record four songs for Peel, released in January 1994 as The Peel Session on Strange Fruit.
years.xp: The EP holds "There's No Other Way/No You Don't," "Bitch Theme," "Make Me Miss America" and "Panik."

years.h: The Real Janelle EP: harder and tighter
years.p: Recorded at Avast in Seattle in July 1993, the six-song EP includes a Misfits cover with Kill Rock Stars co-founder Slim Moon singing.
years.xp: The cover shows Janelle Hessig, a former Bratmobile roadie and East Bay zine maker. AllMusic called it a big step up from the chaotic Pottymouth.

years.big: Best performance art I've ever seen
q: Best performance art I've ever seen.
years.h: Thread Waxing Space: the band breaks up on stage in New York
years.p: At a hyped New York show, women in the crowd take the mic to confront a man in the audience, arguments spread, and Bratmobile break up in the chaos.
years.xp:
KEXP reports Sonic Youth, Joan Jett and Pussy Galore were in the room. Neuman had flown cross-country and slept on the plane. Wolfe later said she was expected to be talent, club manager and security at once.

Spin's Ann Powers wrote that the stoppage lasted at least as long as the set.

eras.title: Two coasts, side projects
eras.text: Neuman heads to the Bay Area and Lookout! Records; Wolfe stays in D.C. and starts a band with Erin Smith. The friendships survive the breakup.

years.h: Cold Cold Hearts: Wolfe and Smith keep playing
years.p: Allison Wolfe and Erin Smith start [[Cold Cold Hearts|092c622c-1c30-4875-bc37-7fac251a8cb1]] in Washington, D.C., with a 7-inch on Kill Rock Stars.
years.xp:
The band ran roughly 1995 to 1998 with drummer Katherine Brown and bassist Nattles. Its catalog is one 7-inch and one self-titled album (1997).

Meanwhile [[Molly Neuman|e4832571-a120-46fb-a5ff-1350f5ed2fce]] moved to the Bay Area, worked at Lookout! Records and played in [[The PeeChees|925ab37f-066e-4c7b-a390-e74df8bf7acd]].

eras.title: Back on Lookout!
eras.text: The trio reunites, tours with Sleater-Kinney and makes two records for Lookout!, the label Neuman co-owns. By 2004 everyone's day jobs win.

years.h: Backstage in D.C., then the Stork Club in Oakland
years.p: Wolfe and Neuman reconnect at a D.C. show where Neuman is managing the Donnas; a low-key Oakland gig relaunches the band, which tours with Sleater-Kinney.
years.xp: Neuman says once they got back together they were friends again almost immediately.

years.h: Ladies, Women and Girls arrives after six years
years.p: Recorded with Tim Green and released on Lookout! Records, with Jon Nikki on bass and keyboards.
years.xp: Rolling Stone said the Brat spirit was fully intact. Pitchfork gave it 6.8 out of 10 and Spin 7.

years.h: Girls Get Busy adds keyboards
years.p: [[Audrey Marrs|d08e65b1-b0f5-406d-a63e-da1abba95d7d]] joins on keys and backing vocals and Marty Violence plays bass on the Lookout! Records album.
years.xp: Reviews split: Pitchfork gave it 4.9, Alternative Press 7 out of 10. Wikipedia credits Marty Key with production alongside Aaron Prellwitz.

years.h: Wolfe posts on the message board: the band is "through"
years.p: There was no formal announcement. Neuman was running Lookout! and managing the Donnas and the Locust, Smith worked at Lookout!, Wolfe had two part-time jobs.
years.xp: Wolfe named her side projects Hawnay Troof, Baby Truth and [[Partyline|cbc09303-767e-4247-83c8-41c26664726c]].

eras.title: Girl Germs, again
eras.text: The band's story gets retold in a podcast, a birthday-party show, festival stages and two reissues.

years.h: Kill Rock Stars releases a Girl Germs podcast about the band
years.p: The label makes a podcast series about Bratmobile called Girl Germs.

years.h: The original trio plays [[Tobi Vail|0a5c5a29-5bcd-4a8b-9ec0-b0c4d2e28851]]'s birthday party
years.p: Wolfe, Neuman and Smith reunite for a show at Tobi Vail's party.

years.h: Mosswood Meltdown: Bratmobile return, with Rose Melberg on guitar
years.p: Wolfe and Neuman reform for Oakland's Mosswood Meltdown with Tiger Trap's Rose Melberg, Audrey Marrs and Marty Key; Erin Smith is unavailable.

years.h: Pitchfork Music Festival, Chicago
years.p: Bratmobile play Union Park; Molly Neuman calls the old songs painfully still relevant.

years.h: Kill Rock Stars reissues Ladies, Women and Girls and Girls Get Busy
years.p: Both Lookout!-era albums come back on the Kill Rock Stars label.
years.xp: Asked about new music, Neuman said it is not a plan right now.

sources.title: KEXP: Throwaway Style, an interview with Bratmobile
